content.user_title: Build a Secure JWT API Client
content.value_statement: JWT API clients can become inconsistent when token refresh, headers, and errors are handled in each component. This skill provides a design framework for a centralized Next.js client with consistent authentication and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Defines a centralized API-client structure for Next.js applications.
Guides Authorization header attachment with Bearer JWT tokens.
Explains token expiry detection and coordinated refresh flows.
Describes consistent parsing for authentication, authorization, and network errors.
Covers client-side, server-side, and React context integration patterns.
Lists security, performance, validation, and testing considerations.
limitations: Provides conceptual guidance, not production-ready source code.
Does not implement an authentication provider or issue JWT tokens.
Does not choose a secure token storage method for your threat model.
Requires you to adapt endpoints, error formats, and framework details.

use_cases.title: Standardize application requests
use_cases.description: Create one API-client approach for a Next.js product with many authenticated endpoints.

use_cases.title: Plan token refresh behavior
use_cases.description: Define how an application refreshes expired tokens and handles failed refresh requests.

use_cases.title: Review client integration
use_cases.description: Check API calls for consistent headers, errors, cancellation, and security practices.

prompt_templates.title: Start an API client plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a simple Next.js API client for my JWT-protected API. Include token attachment and basic error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add refresh handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a token refresh flow for my Next.js API client. Explain how to prevent duplicate refresh requests.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate React access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose a React context and hook interface for a centralized JWT API client.

prompt_templates.title: Review production behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Next.js API-client design for token storage, server and client boundaries, retries, validation, and error exposure.

output_examples.input: Plan a client for authenticated profile and billing endpoints.
output: Central API client with a configurable base URL and request methods.
Bearer token attachment for protected endpoints.
A refresh coordinator that retries eligible requests once.
Typed handling for 401, 403, validation, and network errors.

output_examples.input: Review an existing token refresh approach.
output: Identify where expiration is checked and where refresh begins.
Recommend a single in-flight refresh operation for concurrent requests.
Specify logout and user feedback behavior after a refresh failure.

best_practices: Use HTTPS and validate request parameters before sending them.
Keep token refresh logic centralized and limit retries after refresh failure.
Show safe user messages while keeping sensitive server details out of errors.
anti_patterns: Do not attach tokens to every request without considering endpoint and origin.
Do not start separate token refresh requests for each concurrent API call.
Do not expose raw API errors, tokens, or internal details in the interface.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a complete API client library?
faq.answer: No. It provides conceptual guidance that you adapt to your application.

faq.question: Can this skill manage JWT token refresh?
faq.answer: It explains a refresh design, including coordination and failure handling.

faq.question: Does it support Next.js App Router and Pages Router?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to either router, with adaptation for your execution context.

faq.question: Which token storage method should I use?
faq.answer: Choose storage based on your threat model. The skill does not prescribe one method.

faq.question: Can it handle API errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes consistent handling for authentication, authorization, network, and general errors.

faq.question: Does it replace server-side authorization?
faq.answer: No. The API server must validate tokens and enforce authorization independently.
